brief: The sixth statue standing with open empty hands, a closed carved door behind her base; Śuka narrowing his eyes; Dādī pointing at an inscription with two words kept apart by a small gap; Lubdhaka's foreman scratching his head.

A dark second alcove with a round stone seal cut with a single word and small marks; Dādī pointing at the word; the quarter-visible silver spirit leaning forward; Śuka on her shoulder; Lubdhaka behind with a hand resting on the seal, face calm and unreadable.

The third alcove opened a hand's breadth, with a plain line of script over it; Dādī kneeling and chalking a single root-letter on the stone floor, a neat row of seven flat stones laid beside it like the steps of a wall; the silver spirit nearly whole, watching; Lubdhaka stepping in from the cave mouth with his satchel; Śuka on the stone row.

A mountain cave with four alcoves in the far wall, three dark and the last one glowing behind a sealed round stone; fourteen short lines of script carved above it in a neat row; a small silver spirit of whom only a crescent quarter is visible sitting beside the stone; Dādī and Śuka looking up at the carving; Lubdhaka at the cave mouth with one hand raised, commanding.
